title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for metastatic prostate cancer.

Vitals: BP 138/84, HR 76, RR 16, SpO2 96% on room air, Temp 98.1 F, BMI 26.4.

Recent Labs: Hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, White Blood Cell Count 7.4 x 10^9/L, Platelets 210 x 10^9/L, Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, eGFR 74 mL/min/1.73m2, ALT 42 U/L, AST 38 U/L.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily
- Abiraterone 100 mg daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, or unintended weight loss.
Skin: Denies new rashes or lesions.
Respiratory: Denies shortness of breath or cough.
Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain or jaundice.
Genitourinary: Denies urinary urgency or frequency.
Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain.
Neurological: Denies dizziness or confusion.

Social History: Retired engineer. Lives with his wife. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

HPI: Patient is an 86-year-old male with a history of prostate carcinoma. The primary cancer was removed and treated years ago. Current imaging and clinical evaluation show no evidence of local recurrence at the primary site. The patient is now presenting for management of known liver metastases. He reports mild fatigue but denies acute abdominal pain. He is stable on his current regimen.

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no guarding or rebound. No palpable masses.
Genitourinary: Normal external genitalia.

Assessment:
1. Prostate cancer with liver metastases: The patient has a history of primary prostate carcinoma which was successfully treated years ago. Current assessment shows no evidence of local recurrence at the original site. However, there is evidence of liver metastasis. The patient is currently stable.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications.
2. Monitor liver function and laboratory trends.
3. Follow up in 3 months for repeat imaging and clinical assessment of the liver metastases.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: The prostate cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.46 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
